source: Some scholar challenges every scholar. Therefore every scholar is challenged by some scholar.

claims.interpretation_note: Existential quantifier ('some scholar') followed by universal quantifier ('every scholar')

claims.text: Therefore every scholar is challenged by some scholar.

evidence.quote: Therefore every scholar is challenged by some scholar.

claims.interpretation_note: Universal quantifier ('every scholar') with existential quantifier ('some scholar') in passive voice

translations.formula: (exists x (and (Scholar x) (forall y (implies (Scholar y) (Challenges x y)))))
translations.reason: Existential quantifier for the challenger, universal quantifier for all scholars being challenged

translations.formula: (forall y (implies (Scholar y) (exists x (and (Scholar x) (Challenges x y)))))
translations.reason: Universal quantifier for each scholar being challenged, existential quantifier for the challenger

interpretation_notes: The premise uses an existential quantifier followed by a universal quantifier (∃x∀y), while the conclusion reverses this order (∀y∃x). This quantifier order reversal is a known source of invalidity in first-order logic.
